correctness.rationale: For any continuous common CDF, the transformed endpoints are independent uniforms and have no ties almost surely. Monotonicity then preserves all sampled strict endpoint orders even if the CDF has flat pieces. In the uniform endpoint triangle (u,v), the conditional probabilities of containing a peer and being contained in a peer are respectively (v−u)² and 2u(1−v); others are conditionally independent. Integrating these absence probabilities with density 2 and weight n proves both expectation integrals. For the first, use d=v−u, integrating (1−d²)^(n−1) with weight 2n(1−d); the two terms are n B(1/2,n) and 1. The gamma ratio then gives the stated O(n^(−1/2)) remainder. For the second, integrate in v first, symmetrize u with 1−u, and put s=1−2u on the first half. This gives ∫[1−Q(s)^n]/[1−Q(s)] ds on [0,1] with Q=(1+s²)/2. Expanding the finite series and its binomials gives the claimed sum for all n≥1. To compare with H_n split 2/(1−s²) into 1/(1−s) and 1/(1+s). Since 0≤Q−s=(1−s)²/2 and Q≤exp(−(1−s)/2), the divided power difference integrates to O(1/n); subtracting the Q^n term from the 1/(1+s) integral has O(1/n) cost as well. This proves log n+γ+log 2+O(1/n) and the ratio of expectations only. Independent enumeration of all matchings through seven arcs confirmed both exact means; at n=7 the 135135 matchings give 1619/429 and 140744/45045 respectively. value.rationale: Inner and outer irredundant containment collections are canonical summaries of the same interval sample, not arbitrarily chosen subsets. Exact distribution-free calibration of the logarithmic side, including its constant, and its comparison to the square-root side quantify very different expected summary sizes. This is useful without a claim about concentration or realized ratios; it is not just reusing the known numerical mean of a precedence frontier.
